title: [still present since r3] The 'delivery snap' pin is still non-decisive — an anchor mismatch, not the delivered flag, produces the FALSE
evidence: motion_test.odin:213-218: `p.delivered = true` ... `p.on_edge = false / p.at_node = 2` ... `testing.expect(t, !interp_continuous(&topo, 0, 1, 0, true, &p), "delivered transition must snap")`. Entry (0,1,0,true): the predicate's arrival branch `return entry_heading == p.at_node` evaluates 1 == 2 → false WITHOUT the delivered check; view.odin:176-178 `if p.delivered { return false }` is never the decisive input. PR body line 111-112 claims the opposite: "**W3** — `interp_continuous` now READS `p.delivered` (delivery snaps — the pin tests the predicate, not an incidental anchor mismatch)."
detail: Deleting the delivered guard from interp_continuous leaves every test green — the pin still passes via the same incidental anchor mismatch r3 flagged. The production half shipped; the pin half and the PR-body claim did not.
recommended_fix: Set at_node = 1 (== entry_heading) so arrival would be TRUE absent the flag: then `p.delivered = true` is the only reason the expect holds.
